title: Presentations at work
examples: How many slides should I use for a ten-minute talk?
What is the best way to keep my slides from looking too text-heavy?
Should I put my notes on the slides or just use the speaker notes?

explain.say: A strong presentation needs a clear storyline.

items: Conclusion: Summarize and call to action

explain.say: Every single slide should focus on just one main idea.
Use strong, active verbs to guide your narrative flow.
Keep your visuals clean by using high-quality, relevant images.
Real life example: When presenting a project update, your storyline should move from the problem to your solution.
A common mistake is putting too much text on one slide.

faq.q: How long should my presentation be for a team meeting?
faq.a: For a standard team update, aim for a focused fifteen minutes total. You can also keep it shorter if you are just providing an overview.
asks: What is a good length for a work presentation?
How much time should I allocate?

faq.q: Should I read my slides word for word?
faq.a: No, your slides are visual prompts for you and the audience. You should speak conversationally, expanding on the points shown.
asks: Is it okay to read the slides?
What should I do if I forget what to say?

faq.q: What is the best ratio of text to images?
faq.a: A good guideline is to let the visuals do most of the talking. Use images or graphs to illustrate concepts rather than just describing them with words.
asks: How much picture space do I need?
Should I use more text or more pictures?

faq.q: What does 'call to action' mean in a presentation?
faq.a: It is the single, clear thing you want the audience to do next. You must end by telling them exactly what action is required.
asks: How do I end my talk?
What should my final slide say?

faq.q: Can I use complex data charts?
faq.a: Yes, but simplify them greatly. Only show the data points that directly support your main argument, and label them clearly.

facts: A presentation storyline guides the audience emotionally and logically.
The rule of one idea per slide helps maintain audience focus.
Strong conclusions always include a clear call to action.
Visuals should complement your speech, not repeat it.

quiz.say: If your presentation is about improving efficiency, which structure best guides the audience?

options.say: History to Current State to Future Goals

quiz.why: This structure naturally builds tension by first showing what is wrong before presenting the fix.

wrong.0: This structure lists points but fails to connect them into one cohesive narrative.
wrong.2: This is too academic and doesn't create enough urgency for a business audience.
wrong.3: While informative, this lacks the immediate action focus needed for a persuasive pitch.

quiz.say: Which design principle means limiting each slide to one core concept?
quiz.why: Focusing on one idea prevents cognitive overload for the viewer.

wrong.0: Font size relates to readability, not the conceptual focus of the slide content.
wrong.1: Contrast helps visibility, but it does not enforce the rule of single-idea focus.
wrong.3: Bullet points are a formatting tool, not a guiding principle for content structure.

quiz.say: When concluding, what is the most critical element to include?
quiz.why: The audience must leave knowing exactly what the next step is for them.

wrong.1: While polite, a thank you slide without a clear next step leaves the audience hanging.
wrong.2: Summarizing everything dilutes the impact of the single, most important next step.
wrong.3: This is necessary, but it is secondary to telling them what action to take next.
